snapshot: Nikkei 225 night-session futures closed at 61,410 and TOPIX futures at 3,868, putting the Nikkei future roughly 594 yen above the prior cash close.
Nikkei 225 futures opened at 61,600 at 08:45 JST, setting up a technical rebound after the recent pullback.
Reuters reported USD/JPY at 158.895, the U.S. 10-year yield at 4.591%, and Brent at $109.43. Oil is lower, but still elevated.
The U.S. decision to pause an Iran strike slightly eased geopolitical risk. Japan's January-March GDP grew at an annualized 2.1%, beating expectations.
The market has room to rebound, but rates, oil and FX-intervention risk still matter. Stock selection should favor returns, storage batteries, activism and clean earnings stories.

deep_dive.title: TOKYO BASE: test whether the buyback starting today can keep supporting the tape

lines: The core point is the immediate supply-support effect from a buyback capped at 3.4% of shares and 500 million yen, starting today.
The index is rebounding through futures, but among individual names, an actual return action is the easiest catalyst to validate.
The company announced the buyback after the May 18 close, and the purchase period begins on May 19, allowing the market to test supply support right from the open.
Both Kabutan and Traders Web highlighted the name in morning material coverage, keeping pre-open attention high.
Does real volume appear after the open rather than only an opening-gap reaction.
Does turnover remain stock-specific enough to show this is about TOKYO BASE's supply support rather than the retail sector broadly.
The stock gives back the opening premium once the first buyback reaction is over.
The market judges the buyback size as limited and focuses on the lack of an earnings catalyst.
The buyback is positive, but it is not an earnings upgrade or a dividend increase.
If the broader market turns risk-off again on rates, oil or FX, retail-stock reactions can fade quickly.
